result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A frames the decision more clearly, keeps existing data separate from interviews, and has an explicit section on what a human must do. It also avoids made-up figures and reports findings as 'N of 8'. B is also practical and warns that stated intent is weak evidence, but it adds unsupported benchmarks (an add-on at 8–15% of booking value, click thresholds of 5% and 2%) and never clearly lists the human-only steps. B also squeezes a fake-door test into two weeks, which is a tight fit for the designer's time. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is better. It names the decision the meeting has to make, splits validation into three questions and says what result would mean stopping or going ahead. It also says plainly what a human must do and avoids made-up numbers, reporting results as 'N of 8' instead of percentages. A is practical and gives a clear two-week plan, but it uses figures with no source (an add-on at 8–15% of booking value, click thresholds of 5% and 2%) and never says outright which steps need a person.
